kjv: Out of that land went forth Asshur, and builded Nineveh
mine: From that land he (Nimrod) went out to Assyria and built Nineveh
note: Hebrew yatsa' 'ashshur can mean "Asshur went out" (a person) or "he (Nimrod) went out to Assyria" (accusative of direction); Mic 5:6 links Nimrod to Assyria, favouring the latter. Context: Nimrod went to Assyria (medium confidence). 10:8-12 is a single unit on Nimrod's kingdom, Asshur son of Shem appears only at 10:22, and Mic 5:6 calls Assyria 'the land of Nimrod'; a bare accusative of destination after yatsa' is possible. ESV, NIV, NASB, NRSV, CSB and NET read Nimrod. But every ancient version makes Asshur the subject, so confidence is lowered from high to medium. Other possible meanings: (1) 'Asshur went out (from that land) and built Nineveh', Asshur being a person, ancestor of the Assyrians — LXX, Vulgate, Targum Onkelos, Josephus, KJV, NJPS; (2) the same, with Asshur as the Assyrian people migrating from Babylonia — some commentators.
